sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Project name, commands and libraries
sections.what: Gives the app its name and version, defines the dev, build and start commands, and lists the libraries it uses for the web framework, AI calls, database, login tokens, PDF reading and the interface.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard file, and the one place to see what the app needs.
sections.watch_out: The PDF type helper is listed under normal dependencies. Changing version ranges can change behaviour.

summary: Lists the project name, the commands to run it, and the outside libraries it needs.
purpose: Tells npm which packages to install and which commands to run.
why: Likely reason: this is the standard project file that npm and hosting services read.
how: 1. Install reads the dependency lists and downloads the packages. 2. The dev command starts a local server. 3. The build command makes the production version. 4. The start command runs that version.
inputs: Commands typed by the owner or run by hosting services.
outputs: Installed packages and a running or built app.
risks: Version ranges allow automatic updates that could change behaviour. Next 16 and React 19 are recent, so check compatibility. There is no test or lint command.
debug: If install fails, check the Node version and the lock file. If the build fails on one package, check its version here.
